text.p: British home improvement chain Wickes Plc, rocked last year by an accounting scandal and fraud investigation, on Friday said it had narrowed losses and made a promising start to 1997.

Wickes, whose shareholders in January approved a 53.2 million pounds ($84.7 million) rights issue and capital restructuring to put the troubled group back on its feet, said its pretax loss shrank to 55.7 million pounds last year from 279.3 million a year earlier.

"Managing the recovery from the overstatement of profits provied a tough exercise...The first stage to finance the business is now behind us...and we have made a satisfactory start to 1997," Wickes chief executive Bill Grimsey said in a statement.

Wickes said its planned capital reduction, aimed at freeing up the balance sheet for the future distribution of profits, was expected to be completed by June but no interim dividend for 1997 was expected.

Wickes said sales up to the end of February had risen 13 percent on a like-for-like basis in Britain although continental European turnover was down five percent. Plans to sell off the continental business were under way.

Wickes, which sold its timber, U.S. conservatory and South African businesses last year, said sales dropped to 583.9 million pounds in 1996 from 834.6 million but were up 4.8 percent on the basis of continuing operations. ($ = 0.627 British Pounds)
